[[sn:Brahmaputra River]][[sn:Brahmaputra River]]Literally translated as the, 'son of Brahma',<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OqorAAAAYAAJ&dq=brahmaputra+son+of+brahma&pg=PA387|title=Chambers's Encyclopaedia: A Dictionary of Universal Knowledge|date=1901|publisher=W. & R. Chambers, Limited|pages=387|language=en}}</ref> the legendary origin of the river [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brahmaputra_River Brahmaputra] is featured in the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalika_Purana Kalika Purana]. According to this text, impressed by the piety of a sage named Shantanu and his wife, Amogha, who resided along the banks of the river Lohita, [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brahma Brahma] blessed the couple with his own child in the latter's womb. After his birth, the child took the form of a river, where deities and apsaras would bathe.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Krishna|first=Nanditha|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gp1IDwAAQBAJ&dq=brahmaputra+amogha&pg=PT78|title=Hinduism and Nature|date=2017-12-26|publisher=Penguin Random House India Private Limited|isbn=978-93-87326-54-5|language=en}}</ref>[[Category:Oldest pages before the refresh]]
